XMLDB.COMMENT: The Pro tables as release 2.39.1 declares them. A site upgrading to 3.0.0 still has them and db/upgrade.php still runs on them; a fresh install does not. Upgrade tests install this file to stand where such a site stands.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_rule
TABLE.COMMENT: Automation rules: a trigger, optional conditions, one or more actions. Conditions and actions are JSON arrays rather than child tables, so the schema stays flat and upgrade-safe as new types are added. Phase 8+.

FIELD.NAME: isactive
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=active (rule fires on trigger), 0=disabled.

FIELD.NAME: trigger_type
FIELD.COMMENT: ticket_created | status_changed | time_elapsed | sla_breached

FIELD.NAME: trigger_config
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON params for the trigger, e.g. {"hours":24} for time_elapsed.

FIELD.NAME: conditions
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON array of condition objects: [{type,operator,value}]. Empty = always matches.

FIELD.NAME: actions
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON array of action objects: [{type,value}]. At least one action required.

FIELD.NAME: sort_order
FIELD.COMMENT: Execution order when multiple rules share the same trigger.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_rule_log
TABLE.COMMENT: Automation rule execution log, one row per rule-and-ticket execution attempt. Insert-only. Phase 8+.

FIELD.NAME: triggered_at
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the rule was evaluated.

FIELD.NAME: success
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=all actions executed, 0=partial failure (see note).

FIELD.NAME: note
FIELD.COMMENT: Human-readable result summary or error message.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_email_message
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per email the ingestion pipeline processed. Three jobs: idempotency (unique message_id), threading (in_reply_to and references_header resolve a reply to its ticket without a subject-line token), and an audit trail of email-originated activity. Rows with no ticketid are audit-only, e.g. unknown-sender rejections. Phase 9+.

FIELD.NAME: ticketid
FIELD.COMMENT: Ticket this email belongs to (created or replied to). Null for audit-only rows not tied to a ticket, e.g. unknown-sender rejections (role=3).

FIELD.NAME: replyid
FIELD.COMMENT: Reply row created by this email. Null when this email created the ticket (role=0).

FIELD.NAME: message_id
FIELD.COMMENT: MIME Message-ID header value. Unique. Primary threading key.

FIELD.NAME: in_reply_to
FIELD.COMMENT: MIME In-Reply-To header value. References the direct parent message.

FIELD.NAME: references_header
FIELD.COMMENT: Full MIME References header. Space-separated list of ancestor Message-IDs.

FIELD.NAME: sender_email
FIELD.COMMENT: Sender address, lowercased and trimmed. Used for deduplication and user matching.

FIELD.NAME: sender_name
FIELD.COMMENT: Display name portion of the From header, if present.

FIELD.NAME: raw_subject
FIELD.COMMENT: Original unmodified Subject header value.

FIELD.NAME: role
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=ticket_origin, 1=reply, 2=duplicate_skipped, 3=unknown_sender_rejected, 4=merged_rejected, 5=unauthorised_rejected, 6=unprocessable, 7=token_rejected, 8=token_sender_mismatch, 9=sender_unverified_rejected. See local_moodesk\\domain\\email_message.

FIELD.NAME: reject_reason
FIELD.COMMENT: Reason an email was rejected (e.g. unknown_sender_rejected). Null for accepted emails.

FIELD.NAME: auth_source
FIELD.COMMENT: SEC-04A. What authorised this message to be written into an existing ticket: token | from | none. Null on rows the question does not apply to.

FIELD.NAME: token_status
FIELD.COMMENT: SEC-04A. Outcome of verifying the conversation reply token: valid | absent | foreign_tag | malformed | bad_signature | unknown_key | unknown_version | expired | stale_epoch | sender_mismatch.

FIELD.NAME: token_userid
FIELD.COMMENT: SEC-04A. The user the reply token was issued to. Deliberately distinct from resolved_userid: they are two different facts and must never be collapsed, even when they agree.

FIELD.NAME: resolved_userid
FIELD.COMMENT: SEC-04A. The active Moodle user the declared From address resolved to, if any. The declared address itself is in sender_email.

FIELD.NAME: sender_auth
FIELD.COMMENT: SEC-04B. The authentication verdict derived from the receiving MTA stamp: pass | fail | none | absent | unverifiable | unsupported. NULL means the question was not asked (verification off, or the row predates SEC-04B) and is deliberately distinct from unverifiable, which means it was asked and this site cannot answer it.

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when this email was processed by the task.

FIELD.NAME: ttl_purgedat
FIELD.COMMENT: DATA-01. Unix timestamp when a retention sweep blanked this row's identifying columns. Null means never swept. Only refusal roles are ever swept; see local_moodesk\\domain\\email_message::PURGABLE_AUDIT_ROLES.

INDEX.NAME: uq_message_id
INDEX.COMMENT: Idempotency: prevents double-processing the same email.

INDEX.NAME: ix_sender_timecreated
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports deduplication window query by sender.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_webhook
TABLE.COMMENT: Outbound webhook subscriptions, one row per endpoint. The secret signs the HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Signature-256 header so receivers can verify authenticity. Phase 10+.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Human-readable label, e.g. client name or integration name.

FIELD.NAME: url
FIELD.COMMENT: Target URL for the HTTP POST delivery.

FIELD.NAME: secret
FIELD.COMMENT: HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. Null = no signature sent.

FIELD.NAME: events
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON array of subscribed event types: ticket.created, ticket.updated, ticket.resolved, ticket.replied.

FIELD.NAME: isactive
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=active (dispatch enabled), 0=disabled.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_webhook_log
TABLE.COMMENT: Outbound webhook delivery log, one row per dispatch attempt. success=1 means the endpoint answered 2xx. Insert-only. Phase 10+.

FIELD.NAME: event_type
FIELD.COMMENT: Event that triggered this delivery, e.g. ticket.created.

FIELD.NAME: payload
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON payload sent to the endpoint.

FIELD.NAME: http_status
FIELD.COMMENT: HTTP response code received. Null on connection failure.

FIELD.NAME: response_body
FIELD.COMMENT: First 4 KB of the HTTP response body for debugging.

FIELD.NAME: success
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=HTTP 2xx received, 0=error or non-2xx.

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the delivery was attempted.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_webhook_queue
TABLE.COMMENT: Outbound webhook async dispatch queue, one row per delivery to attempt. The dispatch_webhook task drains rows whose next_retry_at has passed and either marks them done, schedules a retry on the backoff ladder (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h; five attempts maximum), or marks them failed. Successful deliveries also write to local_moodesk_webhook_log.

FIELD.NAME: webhookid
FIELD.COMMENT: Subscription this delivery targets.

FIELD.NAME: event_type
FIELD.COMMENT: Event that triggered this delivery, e.g. ticket.created.

FIELD.NAME: ticketid
FIELD.COMMENT: Originating ticket id, or 0 for non-ticket events.

FIELD.NAME: payload
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON payload to POST to the subscription URL.

FIELD.NAME: attempts
FIELD.COMMENT: Number of delivery attempts made so far.

FIELD.NAME: next_retry_at
FIELD.COMMENT: Earliest unix timestamp at which to attempt delivery.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: Queue state: pending|done|failed.

FIELD.NAME: last_error
FIELD.COMMENT: Most recent failure reason, null on success.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_cfield
TABLE.COMMENT: Custom field definitions for tickets. Definitions only; visibility decides whether requesters see the field or only agents do. Phase 11.C+.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Label shown to users.

FIELD.NAME: description
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional help text shown below the field.

FIELD.NAME: fieldtype
FIELD.COMMENT: text | textarea | select | checkbox | date

FIELD.NAME: options
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON array of option strings. Only used when fieldtype=select.

FIELD.NAME: required
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=required on submission form, 0=optional.

FIELD.NAME: visibility
FIELD.COMMENT: all = shown to requesters and agents; agents_only = hidden from requesters.

FIELD.NAME: sortorder
FIELD.COMMENT: Display order. Lower values appear first.

FIELD.NAME: isactive
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=active (shown on forms), 0=archived (hidden but values preserved).

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_cfield_value
TABLE.COMMENT: Per-ticket values for custom fields, one row per ticket-and-field pair. Values are stored as text whatever the field type; a date is a calendar date as Y-m-d. Phase 11.C+.

FIELD.NAME: value
FIELD.COMMENT: Stored value as string. Date = Y-m-d. Checkbox = 0 or 1.

KEY.NAME: uq_ticket_field
KEY.COMMENT: One value per field per ticket. Enables upsert pattern.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_csat_rating
TABLE.COMMENT: CSAT satisfaction survey, one row per ticket. A NULL rating means the invitation went out and the requester has not answered yet. The token gives the survey page a URL that works from an email link without depending on session state. Phase 11.D+.

FIELD.NAME: ticketid
FIELD.COMMENT: Ticket this survey belongs to. One survey per ticket.

FIELD.NAME: rating
FIELD.COMMENT: 1-5 star rating. NULL = invitation sent but not yet submitted.

FIELD.NAME: comment
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional free-text feedback from the requester.

FIELD.NAME: token
FIELD.COMMENT: Secure random hex token for the survey URL (64 chars).

FIELD.NAME: token_expires
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp after which the token is invalid.

FIELD.NAME: submitted_at
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the requester submitted the rating. NULL = not yet submitted.

INDEX.NAME: uq_token
INDEX.COMMENT: Fast lookup by survey token on the public csat.php page.

INDEX.NAME: ix_submitted_at
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports filtering submitted vs pending surveys in reports.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_team
TABLE.COMMENT: Agent teams for collaborative ticket handling, cross-departmental by design: departments route tickets, teams group agents. A ticket assigned to a team is visible to every member. Phase 11.E+.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Human-readable team name, e.g. Tier 1 Support.

FIELD.NAME: isactive
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=active (visible in assignment dropdowns), 0=archived.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_team_member
TABLE.COMMENT: Agent membership in a team, one row per pair. Only users holding local/moodesk:agent should be added, which the service layer enforces. Phase 11.E+.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Moodle user ID of the agent member.

KEY.NAME: uq_team_user
KEY.COMMENT: One membership record per agent per team.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_api_token
TABLE.COMMENT: mooDesk REST API token metadata (companion to {external_tokens}). Phase 10 (Enterprise).

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Owner of the token. The token inherits this user's capabilities.

FIELD.NAME: externaltokenid
FIELD.COMMENT: The {external_tokens}.id row this metadata augments.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Human-friendly label, e.g. integration or client name.

FIELD.NAME: scopes
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON array of granted scope strings. Stored now, enforced in a later phase.

KEY.NAME: uq_externaltokenid
KEY.COMMENT: One metadata row per native web service token.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_merge_audit
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per merge attempt; immutable except for the revert columns. Phase 12 (Enterprise ticket merge).

FIELD.NAME: sourceticketid
FIELD.COMMENT: Ticket that was merged INTO the target.

FIELD.NAME: targetticketid
FIELD.COMMENT: Canonical ticket that received the source.

FIELD.NAME: actorid
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the agent who executed the merge.

FIELD.NAME: mergedat
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the merge committed.

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional free-text rationale captured at merge time.

FIELD.NAME: source_snapshot
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON snapshot of the source ticket state at merge time (status, priority, departmentid, categoryid, assigneeid, sla_state, custom_fields). Read by revert to restore the source.

FIELD.NAME: migrated_items
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON summary of what was linked: replies, internal notes, attachments, history entries. Counts only, never content.

FIELD.NAME: conflicts
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON list of conflicts encountered, e.g. SLA delta, cross-requester, custom field mismatches.

FIELD.NAME: revertedat
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the revert. NULL while the merge stands.

FIELD.NAME: reverted_actorid
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the agent who reverted. NULL while the merge stands.

FIELD.NAME: ttl_archivedat
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the revert TTL expired and the row became view-only. Rows are never hard-deleted.

INDEX.NAME: ix_mergedat
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports TTL sweeps and chronological audit reporting.

INDEX.NAME: ix_actorid
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports 'what did this agent merge' compliance queries. No foreign key: no plugin table declares one against {user}.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_kb_feedback
TABLE.COMMENT: Was this article helpful? One row per reader per translation row: the reader's current answer, replaced in place when they change their mind. A person's opinion, not the organisation's content — exported under the reader and deleted on erasure. Never purged by retention. KB-07.

FIELD.NAME: articleid
FIELD.COMMENT: The translation row (local_moodesk_kb_article.id) the reader voted on — never the group. Language and group are read from the article at query time, so a re-parented group or a corrected language needs no migration here.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Who voted. The row is deleted, not anonymised, on a privacy erasure request.

FIELD.NAME: helpful
FIELD.COMMENT: 1 yes, 0 no.

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: First vote on this row by this reader.

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Last change of mind; equals timecreated until there is one.

INDEX.NAME: ux_article_user
INDEX.COMMENT: One active vote per reader per translation row; a second vote is an update.

INDEX.NAME: ix_userid
INDEX.COMMENT: Privacy export and erasure by reader.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_kb_event
TABLE.COMMENT: Knowledge base analytics: one anonymous, typed fact per row — a translation was opened, a search found N results, a translation was offered while a ticket was written, opened from there, or shared in a reply. No user id (actorrole is the kind of reader, never the reader), no group or language (read from the article), no JSON. Append-only; purged by two retention windows, one for search rows and one for the rest. KB-07.

FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: 1 view, 2 search, 3 suggest_impression, 4 suggest_open, 5 reply_link. Constants on the kb_event domain class.

FIELD.NAME: articleid
FIELD.COMMENT: The translation row the event is about; NULL for a search, which is about the query.

FIELD.NAME: surface
FIELD.COMMENT: Where it happened: 1 reader (article page), 2 kb_search (landing), 3 composer (Suggested Articles), 4 reply_public, 5 reply_note.

FIELD.NAME: actorrole
FIELD.COMMENT: What kind of person: 0 requester, 1 agent, 2 editor. Never which person.

FIELD.NAME: resultcount
FIELD.COMMENT: Search rows only: how many articles the query found.

FIELD.NAME: querynorm
FIELD.COMMENT: Search rows with resultcount = 0 only: the tokens the engine matched on, lower-cased, redacted of e-mail-like, long-digit and over-long tokens, at most 120 characters. Empty when redaction left nothing. Never a raw query.

INDEX.NAME: ix_type_time_article
INDEX.COMMENT: Every KPI, the day bars and the per-row aggregates: one type over a range, with the article id in the index so a GROUP BY articleid never touches the rows (on MariaDB that was the difference between 6 ms and 650 ms per million events in the KB-07a lab). Also the per-type purge.

INDEX.NAME: ix_type_result_time
INDEX.COMMENT: Searches with no results (type = search, resultcount = 0, range) without touching the row: on MariaDB the row lookups for resultcount cost a second per million events (KB-07a lab).

INDEX.NAME: ix_article_type_time
INDEX.COMMENT: Per-article tables and the delete cascade.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_mailbox_cursor
TABLE.COMMENT: IMAP synchronisation state: one row per polled folder of one mailbox, recording how far the poller has read by UID. The authority on which messages are new (E5); IMAP flags are written for webmail but never read. Holds no personal data: the account is a hash, and no address, subject or Message-ID is stored. Reset, not swept, when the folder's UIDVALIDITY changes.

FIELD.NAME: accountkey
FIELD.COMMENT: sha256 of lower(host):port:lower(user). A different host, port or user is a different mailbox and starts a new cursor.

FIELD.NAME: folder
FIELD.COMMENT: The folder as configured, e.g. INBOX.

FIELD.NAME: uidvalidity
FIELD.COMMENT: The folder's UIDVALIDITY the UIDs below belong to. A different value on SELECT discards them.

FIELD.NAME: lastuid
FIELD.COMMENT: Highest UID the poller has moved past. The next poll searches above it.

FIELD.NAME: retryuids
FIELD.COMMENT: Comma-separated UIDs at or below lastuid that kept failing with a transient error and are retried first on every poll. Bounded; see imap_fetcher.

FIELD.NAME: failuid
FIELD.COMMENT: The UID the cursor is stopped at by a transient error, or 0.

FIELD.NAME: failcount
FIELD.COMMENT: Consecutive polls failuid has failed. At the limit it moves to retryuids and the cursor passes it.

FIELD.NAME: rescanuntil
FIELD.COMMENT: While a one-time re-scan runs: the folder's UIDNEXT when it started, so UIDs below it were already in the folder. 0 when no re-scan is running.

FIELD.NAME: rescansince
FIELD.COMMENT: While a re-scan runs: messages with an IMAP internal date before this time are not read. 0 when no re-scan is running.

INDEX.NAME: ux_account_folder
INDEX.COMMENT: One cursor per folder of one mailbox.
